title: 第19章 裂隙中的抉择第20章 裂隙中的抉择
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
lines: 营房门推开时，陈默看见加雷斯背对着他，站在窗边。
窗外的晚霞正在消退，铅灰色的云层吞没了最后一抹紫色。加雷斯没回头，只是用指节敲了敲窗台。木板上有张羊皮纸，边缘被压得卷起来，上面盖着银月城的火漆印章。
“把门关上。”队长的声音比平时沉。
陈默反手关门，铁锁扣合的声音在狭小的办公室里回荡。他盯着那张羊皮纸，认出上面是调令的格式——他见过类似的，上周有个被派往边境的斥候也拿过同样的纸。
“坐。”加雷斯终于转过身来，脸上没什么表情，但眼角有熬夜留下的血丝。
陈默没坐。他站着，等。
加雷斯拿起那张调令，拇指在羊皮纸边缘停了一瞬——陈默的目光追过去，看见那上面印着铁王国的狼头徽记。队长的拇指正好压在狼头的眼睛上，指腹微微用力，像是要把它按进去。
“教廷的特使，塞西尔，来找过我了。”加雷斯把调令放在桌上，推过来，“他要求你留在城里，随时接受质询。”
陈默没接话。他等着那个“但是”。
“但是——”加雷斯的手指在调令上敲了两下，“我决定把你派出去。边境哨所缺人，铁王国那边的动静不太对。你以增援名义出发，今晚就走。”
陈默低头看着调令。纸上的字迹工整，是书记官的手笔，但最后签名的位置，加雷斯的笔画比平时重。用力到几乎划破纸面。
“这是让我躲开教廷？”陈默问。
“这是让你去干活。”加雷斯的声音冷下来，“边境的‘圣光异常’不止银月城有。铁王国那边，最近三个月，已经有七个哨所报告过类似的现象。教堂里的圣光会突然熄灭，或者——突然燃烧。”
他顿了顿，转身看向窗外。夜色已经完全沉下来，远处的城墙亮起点点灯火。
“教廷内部对你怎么处理，有分歧。”加雷斯说，“有人想直接控制你，有人想把你关起来研究。我选了第三条路——让你去边境，看看那些异常，是不是和你有关。”
陈默盯着加雷斯的背影。这个老骑士的肩膀微微下塌，像扛着什么看不见的重量。
“我是一枚棋子。”陈默说。
“你是。”加雷斯没回头，“但棋子至少还在棋盘上。留在城里，你会被锁进地下室。”
他转过身来，目光锐利如刀：“边境哨所的指挥官是老古斯塔夫。他服役四十年，从不相信圣光。如果你遇到什么——无法理解的事——他可以帮你。”
陈默心头一紧。一个不相信圣光的边境指挥官，在这个圣光至上的帝国里，意味着什么？
“什么时候出发？”他问。
“现在。”加雷斯指了指窗外，“马车在营门外等你。新装备已经准备好了，包括一套——”
他停顿了一下，声音里带着某种说不清的味道：“教廷特别‘改良’过的圣光增幅器。”
陈默感觉后背有电流窜过。那套装备，是监控器。
军械库的地下二层比地面冷得多。
陈默走下石阶时，墙壁上的火把在微微颤抖，像是被什么东西压住了火焰。墙上刻满了抑制圣光的符文，那些线条在火光下扭曲着，像活物一样蠕动。
“这边。”
驼子的声音从阴影里传来。他的身影出现在走廊尽头，手里提着一盏昏黄的油灯。灯芯是黑色的，烧出来的烟带着一股苦涩的药草味。
“队长让我来给你装备。”驼子说，声音压得很低，“跟我来。”
陈默跟着他走进一间密室。房间不大，中间放着一张铁桌，桌上摆着一套崭新的皮甲。皮甲上镶嵌着银色的圣光增幅器，表面刻着细密的符文——和墙上的那些一样，是抑制性质的。
“穿上。”驼子说。
陈默拿起皮甲，指尖触到那些符文时，感觉到一阵微弱的排斥力。圣光在体内躁动了一下，又沉寂下去。
“这套东西不是用来增幅的。”陈默说。
“聪明。”驼子从怀里掏出一个粗糙的皮囊，塞进陈默手里，“这个，才是真正有用的。”
皮囊不大，摸起来软软的，里面装着某种干燥的颗粒。陈默打开口子，一股苦涩的气味冲进鼻腔——是药草，但和他认识的任何一种都不一样。
“这是什么？”
“灰烬沼泽的苦艾。”驼子压低声音，“老古斯塔夫的暗语。你到了边境，把这东西给他看，他会明白。”
陈默握着皮囊，感觉到一股与圣光截然不同的力量在掌心流动。那力量沉郁、厚重，像从地底深处涌上来的泉。
“圣光是一种交易。”驼子盯着陈默的眼睛，“不是恩赐。你用得越多，它要的也越多。这药草能暂时压制圣光的灼烧，但——”
他停顿了一下，声音更低了：“治标不治本。”
陈默想起圣光失控时，那种从骨髓里涌出来的灼热感。理智被侵蚀的声音，像砂纸在骨头上打磨。
content_en:
When the barracks door opened, Chen Mo saw Gareth standing by the window with his back to him.
The sunset outside the window is fading, and the leaden clouds have swallowed up the last trace of purple. Gareth didn't look back, just rapped his knuckles on the window sill. There is a piece of parchment on the wooden board, the edges are pressed and rolled up, and it is stamped with the fire seal of Silvery Moon City.
"Close the door." The captain's voice was deeper than usual.
Chen Mo closed the door with his backhand, and the sound of the iron locks closing echoed in the small office. He stared at the parchment and recognized the format of a transfer order - he had seen something similar, and a scout sent to the border had taken the same paper last week.
"Sit." Gareth finally turned around, his face expressionless, but there were bloodshot eyes from staying up late.
Chen Mo didn't sit down. He stood, waiting.
Gareth picked up the transfer order and paused with his thumb on the edge of the parchment for a moment - Chen Mo followed it with his eyes and saw the Iron Kingdom's wolf head emblem printed on it. The captain's thumb was pressed just on the wolf's eye, and his fingertips were slightly pressed, as if he was trying to press it in.
"The special envoy of the Holy See, Cecil, came to see me." Gareth put the transfer order on the table and pushed it over. "He asked you to stay in the city and accept questioning at any time."
Chen Mo didn't answer. He waited for the "but."
"But -" Gareth's finger tapped twice on the transfer order, "I have decided to send you out. The border post is short of people, and there is something wrong with the movement in the Iron Kingdom. You set out in the name of reinforcements and leave tonight."
Chen Mo lowered his head and looked at Tiao Ling. The handwriting on the paper was neat, the handwriting of the clerk, but where Gareth's signature was placed at the end, Gareth's strokes were heavier than usual. So hard that it almost broke the paper.
"Are you asking me to avoid the Holy See?" Chen Mo asked.
"This is for you to go to work." Gareth's voice became colder. "Silver Moon City is not the only one with the 'holy light anomaly' on the border. Over in the Iron Kingdom, seven outposts have reported similar phenomena in the past three months. The holy light in the church will suddenly go out, or - suddenly burn."
He paused and turned to look out the window. The night has completely fallen, and the city wall in the distance is lit up with lights.
"There are differences within the Holy See on how to deal with you." Gareth said. "Some people want to control you directly, and some want to lock you up for research. I chose the third way - let you go to the border to see if those anomalies are related to you."
Chen Mo stared at Gareth's back. The old knight's shoulders slumped slightly, as if he was carrying some invisible weight.
"I am a chess piece." Chen Mo said.
"You are." Gareth didn't look back, "But at least the chess pieces are still on the chessboard. If you stay in the city, you will be locked in the basement."
He turned around, his eyes as sharp as knives: "The commander of the border post is old Gustav. He has served for forty years and has never believed in the Holy Light. If you encounter something - something you cannot understand - he can help you."
Chen Mo's heart tightened. What does a border commander who doesn't believe in the Holy Light mean in this empire where the Holy Light is supreme?
"When are you leaving?" he asked.
"Now." Gareth pointed out the window, "The carriage is waiting for you outside the camp gate. New equipment has been prepared, including a set of -"
He paused, and there was something inexplicable in his voice: "The Holy Light Amplifier specially 'improved' by the Holy See."
Chen Mo felt an electric current running through his back. That piece of equipment is a monitor.
***
The second underground level of the armory is much colder than the ground.
When Chen Mo walked down the stone steps, the torch on the wall trembled slightly, as if something was suppressing the flame. The walls were engraved with runes that suppressed the Holy Light, and those lines twisted in the firelight, squirming like living creatures.
"This way."
The hunchback's voice came from the shadows. His figure appeared at the end of the corridor, holding a dim oil lamp in his hand. The wick is black, and the smoke has a bitter herbal smell.
"The captain asked me to equip you." The hunchback said in a low voice, "Follow me."
Chen Mo followed him into a secret room. The room was not big, with an iron table in the middle and a brand new set of leather armor on the table. The leather armor is inlaid with a silver Holy Light Amplifier, and the surface is engraved with fine runes - the same inhibitory properties as those on the wall.
"Put it on," said the hunchback.
Chen Mo picked up the leather armor and felt a weak repulsive force when his fingertips touched the runes. The holy light stirred in the body for a moment, then fell silent.
"This set of things is not used to increase the gain." Chen Mo said.
"Smart." The hunchback took out a rough leather bag from his arms and stuffed it into Chen Mo's hand, "This is the one that is really useful."
The skin bag is not big, feels soft, and contains some kind of dry particles. Chen Mo opened his mouth, and a bitter smell rushed into his nose - it was medicinal herbs, but it was different from any kind he knew.
"What is this?"
"The wormwood in the Ash Swamp." The hunchback lowered his voice, "Old Gustav's code word. When you get to the border, show him this thing, and he will understand."
Chen Mo held the skin bag and felt a power completely different from the holy light flowing in his palm. The power was deep and heavy, like a spring rising from the depths of the earth.
"The Holy Light is a transaction." The hunchback stared into Chen Mo's eyes, "It is not a gift. The more you use it, the more it wants. This herb can temporarily suppress the burning of the Holy Light, but -"
He paused and said in a lower voice: "Treating the symptoms, not the root cause."
Chen Mo thought of the burning feeling that surged from his bones when the Holy Light lost control. The sound of sanity being eroded is like sandpaper being rubbed against bones.
